events.title: Storytime with Claire Wrenn Bobrow
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Claire Wrenn Bobrow returns to Linden Tree to share her delightful new picture book, Party Pony! Not another party! Parties used to be Pony's favorite—until every bash turned him into a work horse! Now Pony is a party pooper. How will Pony's friends show him he's worthy of a party too? For any kid who's ever felt left out, this witty picture book is a must-have for the home or school library, and it's perfect for gifting and reading at parties. Grab your copy and join the celebration!
events.blurb: Hear author Claire Wrenn Bobrow read her new picture book "Party Pony!" and find out why the pony has grown tired of parties.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We aim to introduce readers to new books they can discuss together in a fun, relaxed setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Home Scientist (Brownies)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Science is all around us! Brownies begin by making pepper dance using the amazing properties of electricity. Next, they become kitchen chemists and use pantry items to make art with delicious treats. Then they explore properties of density and use them to blow up a balloon without breath and make their own lava lamp. Finally, Brownies will learn how science can be used to make toys and make their very own silly putty! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Home Scientist Badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Make pepper dance with electricity, then use pantry items as a kitchen chemist in this Brownies Home Scientist program.

events.title: Girl Scout Program: Tech Detective (Juniors and Cadettes)
events.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Do you have what it takes to be a Tech Detective? Juniors and Cadettes will begin by practicing the art of forensic drawing by sketching a "suspect" as described by a "key witness." Next, they learn about & practice codes and fingerprinting. Juniors will explore the role of DNA in forensics — what it is, what it does, and how it helps solve crimes. They then get to perform an experiment to extract real DNA, and finally use what they have learnt to identify someone from ancient DNA! This program covers all five steps required to earn the Juniors Detective badge or the Cadette Special Agent badge. Participants will receive the badge and a Tech fun patch at the end of the session.
events.blurb: Sketch a "suspect" from a key witness's description, then practice forensic drawing, codes, and fingerprinting as a Junior or Cadette Girl Scout.

events.title: Storytime with Sahar Shams
events.description: Join us for a special storytime as author Sahar Shams shares her festive debut picture book, What Does Santa Want for Christmas? Every year, children all around the world ask themselves what they'd like to receive from Santa. But one little boy has a different question: What would Santa wish for? Determined, Dorim sets out on a quest to craft the perfect present—but he'll need some help from his friends. With Christmas fast approaching, will they be able to make Santa's wish come true in time?

events.title: Location Change: Mindfulness Meditation
events.venue: Palo Alto Art Center, Meeting Room
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience, and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. See the library's event page to learn more about Phuong and find her videos on the library's YouTube channel.

events.title: Asistencia para Búsqueda de Trabajo
events.description: ¿Buscas apoyo para avanzar en tu carrera? ¡Estamos aquí para ayudarte! Te guiamos para encontrar vacantes en los principales sitios web de trabajo. Te ayudamos a completar solicitudes, verificar tu historial laboral y preparar otros documentos esenciales para tu contratación. events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines
events.description: Help keep the library clean and welcoming. The library credits $20 toward your fines for each hour you volunteer. Volunteers will clean book covers with disinfecting wipes, dust shelves, and organize library materials. They will also use disinfecting wipes on computer mice and mouse pads, clear dust and debris with compressed air, and check books for damage such as torn pages or pen marks. Volunteers must commit to the full session. Anyone under 15 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. No experience or special skills are needed. Training and supplies will be provided. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Register online. For help registering, call or visit the library's information desk. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Work off your library fines by volunteering to help keep the Alviso Library clean and welcoming.

events.title: Community Game & Craft Day
events.description: Whether you're looking to meet new people, learn a new game, make progress on a craft, or simply spend a relaxing afternoon with fellow hobbyists, there's a place for you at Community Game and Craft Day. No experience is necessary—just bring your enthusiasm and join the fun! This event takes place in the library community room. Tables and chairs are provided. Bring your favorite board games, card games, role-playing games, crafting projects, works-in-progress, or creative projects to share and enjoy. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Learn new games, work on a craft, and meet other hobbyists at this open community day.

events.title: Community Yoga and Heartfulness Meditation
events.description: Experience the soothing calm of yoga and meditation, as presented by our partner, The Heartfulness Institute, each Saturday. Yoga is taught by certified instructors and meditation is taught by a Heartfulness-certified instructor. Yoga may be either chair or regular yoga. The program structure is 75 minutes as described below: 5 min: Meet & greet; 35 min: Yoga and Pranayama (different styles like hatha or arkaya yoga); 5 min: posture change break; 25 min: Heartfulness Relaxation & Meditation (experience, hands-on). events.title: Easy Tech Seniors
events.description: Learn new skills in a relaxed and interactive group setting! Easy Tech Seniors is led by Malhar, a local high school student with a passion for helping senior citizens embrace technology to enrich their daily lives. For the best experience, we recommend bringing your own mobile device, but you can also follow the demonstration on the projector screen and take notes. 2026 Topics: Jan 24th - Library apps for reading e-books - an overview of SJPL's e-book collections on the library website, with a focus on Libby from OverDrive - How to adjust reading settings like text size and lighting, and how to use the audiobook controls. If time allows, the session will also cover Hoopla. Feb 28th - Using Zoom for Meetings and Social Connection - How to join meetings confidently or host simple meetings. Learn to mute and unmute audio or video and use the chat. Troubleshooting basics will also be covered. Mar 28th - Using ChatGPT - How to use ChatGPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using ChatGPT responsibly will also be covered. April 25th - Managing contacts effectively and setting reminders - Add and organize contacts on your device. Create groups (family, emergency). Back up and sync safely. Set recurring reminders for daily tasks. Integrate reminders with calendars. May 23rd - Demystifying AI. June 27th - Spotting AI Scams and Fake Messages. July 25th - Emergency Features on Smartphones. August 22nd - Google Translate for Travel and Communication - Use text, voice, and camera translation. Save common phrases for travel. Practice offline translation. September 26th - Using ChatGPT - How to use ChatGPT to summarize long documents, organize items like receipts, ask effective questions and protect your privacy. Using ChatGPT responsibly will also be covered. October 24th - How to Make Your Phone Easier to See - Adjusting text size, using the magnifier, voice to text, and dark mode. On November 28, learn to turn on and use Siri or Google Assistant. Practice checking the weather, setting timers, and making calls. You'll also learn to manage privacy settings and shortcuts. There is no program in December. The class is free and limited to 10 attendees. Registration is recommended. Walk-ins are welcome if space is available.
events.attendanceNote: Online reservations are recommended. Walk-ins are welcome if space is available.

events.title: Queer Cafe - Cozy Vibes Edition
events.description: Queer joy shall abound at the Queer Café! Let's grab our chunky knit sweaters, a warm cup of something pumpkin-spiced, and celebrate the fall season for November's Queer Cafe. Queer Cafe is an LGBTQ+-friendly space in our community room for folks to gather, read, craft, and chat. A selection of queer reading materials will be available to browse and check out. In addition to light snacks and refreshments, we'll have craft supplies and a selection of cozy and found family reads highlighting queer characters and authors. While the intention of this program is to create a safe and comfortable space for patrons identifying as LGBTQ+, we welcome all participants and reading materials. ¡La alegría queer estará presente en cada rincón del Café Queer! ¡Pongámonos nuestros suéteres gruesos de punto, disfrutemos de una bebida calientita con especias de calabaza y celebremos la temporada de otoño en el Café Queer de noviembre! El Café Queer es un espacio acogedor para la comunidad LGBTQ+ en nuestra sala comunitaria, donde las personas pueden reunirse, leer, hacer manualidades y conversar. Habrá una selección de libros y otros materiales de lectura con temática LGBTQ+ disponibles para explorar y llevar en préstamo. Además de bocadillos y bebidas ligeras, tendremos materiales para manualidades y una selección de lecturas reconfortantes, incluidas historias sobre familias elegidas, que destacan a personajes y autores LGBTQ+. Se anima a las personas participantes a compartir y conocer a otros lectores con intereses similares, pero no se les pedirá que revelen su identidad ni sus preferencias de lectura. Aunque el propósito de este programa es crear un espacio seguro y cómodo para las personas que se identifican como LGBTQ+, todas las personas y todos los materiales de lectura son bienvenidos.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes.

events.title: Social Workers in the Library Drop-In Hours
events.description: Advice, information, and referrals. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Staff can meet with you without judgment and help you find shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We'll do our best to connect you with resources that meet your needs. Asesoramiento, información y referencias. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades. Tư vấn, thông tin và giới thiệu. Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn.

events.title: Math Buddies
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Math Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their math skills by working one-on-one with a volunteer. At Math Buddies, volunteers sit with participating children for an individual 15- to 20-minute tutoring session. Volunteers may help participants complete math homework assignments or math worksheets provided by Math Buddies volunteers. Math Buddies creates a positive learning experience for students who may be struggling with math or lack confidence as math students. Free. No advance registration is required. Tutoring is first come, first served. The number of sessions may depend on how many volunteers and children attend.

events.description: Join Las Madres Downtown/Rose Garden for a weekly Tuesday playgroup. Children can play in a safe environment in the Rose Garden Library Community Room, and parents can meet and support one another in the Rose Garden and downtown San José area. This is a free event. No registration is required. Las Madres Neighborhood Playgroups is a volunteer-run nonprofit. Las Madres offers playgroups for parents and children, organized by children's ages and by neighborhood clubs. The organization is based in Santa Clara County, California. "Nothing substitutes for the ability to build friendships with parents who are faced with similar parenting issues."
events.blurb: At this weekly playgroup, children can play in the Rose Garden Library Community Room while local parents meet and support one another.

events.title: Teens Reach
events.description: Teens Reach is the San José Public Library's youth council for ages 13–18. Members build leadership skills by organizing and taking part in library activities and serving as library advisors and advocates. Develop your leadership skills by providing ideas for programming, events, displays, etc., and actively helping to bring these ideas to life. If you are new to volunteering with the San Jose Public Library, please visit the Teens Reach: Community Service webpage for more information and be sure to create your online volunteer account.
events.blurb: Join teens ages 13-18 to plan library activities and build leadership skills with the Teens Reach youth council.

events.description: Join us for Music and Movement storytime. Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. It is a fun, interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joy of learning for all ages. This program is best suited for children ages 2 to 5, accompanied by their families or caregivers. We'll move and groove to our action songs using shakers, tapping sticks, scarves, and more, and listen to fun and educational stories. We will also meet our favorite Teddy Bear. Free, with limited capacity. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes before storytime starts. The program is held in the Community Room on the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays of the month. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

events.title: ELL Advanced English: Writing Club
events.description: English Language Learners (ELL) can practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. The club meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesdays of each month and on the 5th Tuesday when there is one. Topics may include creating simple sentence structures, learning some basic grammar, and building up to writing a simple paragraph. Suggested for high beginners up to advanced English language learners. Space is limited and registration is required. Please stop by the Vineland Library or call us at (408) 808-3000 to register. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Grammar and Vocabulary Club: An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Conversation Club: An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where English learners at levels from high beginner to advanced can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited and registration is required.

events.description: Are you a budding creative writer? Whether you've written for years or started yesterday, register for fresh inspiration to make your story shine! Young writers in 2nd through 5th grade (ages 7-11) are invited to join us for this creative writing workshop series hosted at the Pearl Avenue Branch Library. Attendees will learn to make their fiction feel real, create characters that hold readers' attention, and identify plot points that work across genres. This series will run from Tuesday, May 5th to Tuesday, December 15th, 2026. Register for each session you plan to attend. Free. Registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library.
events.blurb: Bring your work in progress and get fresh inspiration to sharpen your storytelling.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) 502: Listening & Speaking
events.description: ESL Listening & Speaking 1 is a noncredit course for high-beginning English learners. Students will learn to pronounce basic words accurately, communicate effectively, understand and use basic grammar structures, and build their foundational vocabulary. To enroll, complete and pass the Self-Guided Computer Assessment. This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. For accurate results, complete the assessment on your own in a quiet setting. Submit the registration form. To schedule your assessment appointment, send an email to marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org. ESL 502 runs from August 25, 2026, through December 10, 2026. Classes meet Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 5:15 PM to 6:45 PM. The instructor is to be determined. We will assist you with the application and registration processes in person at the Educational Park Branch Library. Space is limited. ESL Escucha y Conversación 1 (curso de ESL sin crédito, nivel básico alto). Los estudiantes aprenden a pronunciar palabras básicas, a comunicarse de manera efectiva, a usar estructuras gramaticales simples y a ampliar su vocabulario. Para inscribirte, completa y aprueba la evaluación autoguiada en computadora. No es un examen. La evaluación nos ayuda a asignarte a la clase de ESL más adecuada para tu nivel de inglés. Para obtener resultados precisos, hazla sin ayuda y en un lugar tranquilo. Completa el formulario de inscripción. Envía un correo electrónico a marcela.guevara@sjlibrary.org para programar una cita para la evaluación. El curso ESL 502 comienza el 25 de agosto de 2026 y termina el 10 de diciembre de 2026. Las clases son los martes, miércoles y jueves de 5:15 p.m. a 6:45 p.m. El instructor está por definir. Te ayudaremos con los procesos de solicitud y registro en persona en la Biblioteca Educational Park. El espacio es limitado.

events.title: Bilingual Toddler Storytime / Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play
events.description: Bilingual Toddler Storytime is designed for toddlers to engage in early literacy activities such as stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement. While the program is geared toward children ages 1–3, all children ages 0–5 are welcome to attend. After Storytime concludes, families are invited to Stay & Play. For 30 minutes after storytime, children and caregivers can keep playing with age-appropriate toys. Storytime runs from 11:30 a.m. to noon. Stay & Play runs from noon to 12:30 p.m. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play: Tiempo de Cuentos está diseñado para niños pequeños e invita a toda la familia a participar en actividades de alfabetización temprana, como cuentos, rimas, juegos con los dedos y actividades de movimiento. Después de que concluya el Tiempo de Cuentos, las familias están invitadas a quedarse y jugar. Durante 30 minutos después del Tiempo de Cuentos, habrá juguetes especiales y apropiados para cada edad disponibles para continuar la diversión. Tiempo de cuentos: de 11:30 a.m. a 12:00 p.m. Stay & Play: de 12:00 p.m. a 12:30 p.m. Este programa se diseñó de acuerdo con los Estándares de Calidad de la Educación Infantil.
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and play with your toddler during this bilingual early literacy storytime.

events.title: Asistencia tecnológica y ayuda personalizada
events.description: ¿Quieres aprender a usar la tecnología por tu cuenta? Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarte a un punto de acceso o a una red Wi-Fi; Usar Chromebooks o computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar clases de la biblioteca e inscribirte en ellas; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Usar un teléfono móvil; Buscar en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estará allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puedes asistir a tu cita, llama para cancelarla. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere inscripción. Para inscribirte, llama al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Get personalized tech help in Spanish at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana and practice doing the tasks yourself.

events.title: Asistencia para buscar trabajo y crear un resumen (currículum)
events.description: ¿Necesita ayuda con su currículum o para buscar oportunidades de empleo? Reúnase en persona con un miembro del personal de la biblioteca para recibir ayuda individual. Puede crear o actualizar su currículum, usar sitios web de solicitudes de empleo, completar solicitudes y practicar técnicas de entrevista. events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: We'll be reading Elatsoe by Darcie Little Badger in honor of Native American Heritage Month. Sign up at the adult reference desk to get a copy. "Imagine an America very similar to our own. It's got homework, best friends, and pistachio ice cream. There are some differences. This America has been shaped dramatically by the magic, monsters, knowledge, and legends of its peoples, those Indigenous and those not. Some of these forces are charmingly everyday, like the ability to make an orb of light appear or travel across the world through rings of fungi. But other forces are less charming and should never see the light of day. Seventeen-year-old Elatsoe ("Ellie" for short) lives in this slightly stranger America. She can raise the ghosts of dead animals, a skill passed down through generations of her Lipan Apache family. Her beloved cousin has just been murdered, in a town that wants no prying eyes. But she is going to do more than pry. The picture-perfect façade of Willowbee masks gruesome secrets, and she will rely on her wits, skills, and friends to tear off the mask and protect her family." For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3947, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

The public sale runs Friday, December 4, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Saturday, December 5, from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Bargain Day is Sunday, December 6. The sale is open to the public from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Other ongoing Friends of the Milpitas Library sales include the Book Nook. We have a variety of great books available at great prices every day in the Book Nook behind the accounts desk on the first floor. All books are 50% off every Sunday. events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces
events.description: Are you experiencing the "holiday guest stress syndrome"? Don't let the pressure of having a perfect tablescape wilt your holiday spirit! Join UC Master Gardeners Laura Westley, Sue Neufeld, and Bernie Day for an inspiring, hands-on demonstration designed to take the stress—and the high cost—out of holiday decorating. You don't need a professional florist or a massive budget to create a "wow" factor for your dining room. What You'll Learn: The Art of the "Found" Object: Learn how to scout your own backyard or junk drawer for unique textures, greenery, and accents that add character to any arrangement. Grocery Store Glam: Discover how to deconstruct those affordable supermarket flower bunches and reimagine them into high-end-looking centerpieces. Pro-Tips for Longevity: Get the inside scoop on keeping your flora fresh from the first toast to the final slice of pie. Why join us? Whether you're hosting a grand feast or an intimate gathering, you'll walk away with the confidence and practical skills to transform "ordinary" items into extraordinary focal points. events.title: CNPS Talk #3: The birds, the bees, and a magic trait: The evolution of red hummingbird flowers in California, a talk by Prof. Justen Whittall
events.description: Why are so many of California's favorite hummingbird flowers red? From California fuchsia blooming in the fall to western columbine, scarlet bugler, and Indian paintbrush, our native flora is full of brilliant red flowers that hummingbirds love. But is red simply a color that attracts hummingbirds, or does it also help flowers avoid unwanted visits from bees? Join Santa Clara University biology professor Justen Whittall to explore how hummingbirds and bees see flowers differently, including a hidden world of ultraviolet colors invisible to humans. Drawing on recent research with his students and international collaborators, he'll reveal how these hidden pigments may help explain not only why hummingbird flowers are red, but also how new plant species evolve. Speaker Biography: Justen Whittall was born in Santa Clara and earned his B.S. in Biology from Santa Clara University, an M.S. from Oregon State University studying monkeyflower conservation genetics, and a Ph.D. from UC Santa Barbara investigating the evolution of California columbines. Following postdoctoral research at UC Davis on the evolution of California's serpentine-endemic plants, including blue-eyed Mary, wallflowers, and jewelflowers, he returned to SCU in 2007 as a professor of Biology. He works closely with undergraduates to uncover the mysteries of plant ecology and evolution, with research ranging from the conservation of rare Santa Clara County plants—including jewelflowers, columbines, liveforevers, and Hoita—to the evolution of flower color and hummingbird pollination in California's native flora. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: The group picks a graphic novel to discuss each month. The club is open to readers ages 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA. October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation. November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County. January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA. April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. The story follows a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Borrow the books from Palo Alto City Library or through Link+. Search the library catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. events.title: Non-Fiction Book Discussion – Finders Keepers: a Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession
events.description: In December, the Cupertino Library's nonfiction book group will discuss Craig Childs' 2010 book Finders Keepers: A Tale of Archaeological Plunder and Obsession. Journalist Craig Childs documents his efforts to find and preserve precious and ancient artifacts from the American Southwest that could help answer questions about the people who made and used them. From archaeological digs in the deserts of Arizona and New Mexico to high-end art galleries and museums in New York and Boston, Childs had to protect the artifacts and himself from ruthless art smugglers, risking his life and freedom multiple times. Childs' book also asks who owns the past and its archaeological finds. An archaeologist may be praised for excavating an ancient site and sharing their finds with a famous museum. Someone who takes a precious relic from a museum because they believe it is sacred and belongs where it was found is called a thief. Which one is in the wrong? The Non-fiction Book Discussion group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am. All meetings are held in Room 201B. Sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. events.title: Animal Friends: Meet a Chicken with Isabelle Cnudde
events.description: Did you know chickens can recognize over 100 faces, dream when they sleep, and even see more colors than we do? Join Project Humane Kind at the Palo Alto Children's Library as we meet Clorofil's Isabelle Cnudde and one of her feathered friends. Come discover their natural behaviors, their big personalities, and what makes them such cool animals. Coloring pages will be available for the attendees. Registration required. Note: Registrations will be released for standby attendees at the start of the program. Please arrive on time. As founder of Clorofil, an animal advocacy nonprofit and micro-sanctuary, Isabelle rescues chickens and gives them a safe home where they can just be chickens. Learn more about them at www.clorofil.org. Project Humane Kind teaches compassion and respect for living beings. Through humane education, they combat cruelty and indifference and bring awareness to the intelligent, social, and emotional depths of our fellow animals. Visit them online at www.projecthumanekind.org.

events.title: Adult Book Discussion: True Grit by Charles Portis
events.description: In December, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will discuss the novel True Grit by Charles Portis (1968). As a teenager in the 1870s, Mattie Ross needs help finding her father's murderer, Tom Chaney, who belongs to a notorious outlaw gang. She hires the washed-up marshal Rueben T. "Rooster" Cogburn, believing he has the true grit for the dangerous job and that his reputation for violence will help. He agrees to help out of a desperate need for money. A Texas Ranger joins them. He also wants to bring Chaney back to Texas for an earlier murder and collect the "dead or alive" reward. Despite their different motivations, the three of them are a team by the time they finally track Chaney and the gang down. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month, on the third Wednesday morning at 11 AM, and the third Thursday evening at 7 PM. All meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Celebrating Yalda Night
events.description: Join us for a special Yalda Night celebration with children's author Anahita Tamaddon and a reading of her book, Yalda Night! Experience the beauty of this cherished Persian tradition through a Yalda-inspired story, music, and a fun paper craft featuring one of Yalda's beloved symbols. Yalda, the longest night of the year, is a joyful celebration of family, storytelling, and togetherness as we welcome the arrival of winter. All craft materials will be provided. Children ages three and up, along with their adult caregivers, are invited to participate. Materials will be available while supplies last. While registration isn't required and doesn't guarantee a spot, it is recommended if you'd like a reminder about the event. برای جشن ویژه‌ی شب یلدا همراه با نویسنده‌ی کتاب‌های کودک، آناهیتا تمدن، به ما بپیوندید. در این برنامه با زیبایی‌های این سنت دیرینه‌ی ایرانی از طریق قصه‌ای با حال‌وهوای یلدا، موسیقی و ساخت کاردستی کاغذی با الهام از یکی از نمادهای دوست‌داشتنی یلدا آشنا خواهیم شد. شب یلدا، بلندترین شب سال، فرصتی برای جشن گرفتن در کنار خانواده و عزیزان، قصه‌گویی و با هم بودن و همچنین خوشامدگویی به فصل زمستان است. تمام وسایل مورد نیاز برای ساخت کاردستی فراهم خواهد بود.

events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for guided sitting and releasing meditation, followed by group sharing and Q&A.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: NeuroSphere: Neuroscience and More!
events.description: Come join the teen-led group NeuroSphere! This session will dive into the basics of brain function, fun activities to test your brainpower, and an introduction to future career opportunities. Our mission is to inspire curiosity and spark a love for science in younger students by creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences. Through NeuroSphere, we hope to share our knowledge, connect with the community, and encourage the next generation of future scientists and innovators! Questions? Email neurosphereyouth@gmail.com.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: The group picks a graphic novel to discuss each month. The club is open to readers ages 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA. October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation. November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County. January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA. April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. The story follows a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Borrow the books from Palo Alto City Library or through Link+. Search the library catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners
events.description: Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. Members suggest books and vote on what to read next. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: The group picks a graphic novel to discuss each month. The club is open to readers ages 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA. October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation. November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County. January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA. April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. The story follows a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Borrow the books from Palo Alto City Library or through Link+. Search the library catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join the Graphic Novel Book Club at Mitchell Park Library to discuss the group's latest pick, Thursday evenings.

events.title: Pageturners: Double Play on the Red Line by Raj Oza
events.description: Join us for a special discussion with local author Raj Oza about his book Double Play on the Red Line. Ask Oza about his writing process and how the novel came about. Pageturners read widely, from nonfiction like Palo Alto: A History of California, Capitalism, and the World by Malcolm Harris to fiction like James by Percival Everett to biography like The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI by Fei-Fei Li and graphic novels like The Best We Could Do by Thi Bui. Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. Members suggest books and vote on what to read next. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. You don't have to register, but you will receive a reminder email if you do.
events.blurb: Hear local author Raj Oza discuss how he came to write Double Play on the Red Line.

events.title: Documentary Screening – Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space
events.description: Join us for a screening of the PBS documentary Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space, about a major Black American writer. Hurston is best known for her novel Their Eyes Were Watching God. The film explores her work as an anthropologist and how it influenced her writing. From the producer: "Raised in the small all-Black Florida town of Eatonville, Zora Neale Hurston studied at Howard University before arriving in New York in 1925. She would soon become a key figure of the Harlem Renaissance, best remembered for her novel, Their Eyes Were Watching God. But even as she gained renown in the Harlem literary circles, Hurston was also discovering anthropology at Barnard College with the renowned Franz Boas. She would make several trips to the American South and the Caribbean, documenting the lives of rural Black people and collecting their stories. She studied her own people, an unusual practice at the time, and during her lifetime became known as the foremost authority on Black folklore. Directed by Tracy Heather Strain, produced by Randall MacLowry and executive produced by Cameo George, Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space is an in-depth biography of the influential author whose groundbreaking anthropological work would challenge assumptions about race, gender and cultural superiority that had long defined the field in the 19th century." Interested in delving deeper into Hurston's work? Join us for February's Short Story Social the Thursday following the screening to discuss her short story "Sweat."
events.blurb: Watch the PBS documentary Zora Neale Hurston: Claiming a Space at a library screening. The film explores how Hurston's work as an anthropologist informed her writing.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club: Women's History Month
events.description: The group picks a graphic novel to discuss each month. The club is open to readers ages 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA. October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation. November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County. January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA. April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. The story follows a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Borrow the books from Palo Alto City Library or through Link+. Search the library catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph.D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/
events.blurb: Join a monthly discussion of a group-chosen graphic novel at Mitchell Park Library, open to readers age 16 and up.

events.title: Pageturners

Local authors like Mike Trigg, Susie Hara and Olga Zilberbourg and visiting International Booker Prize winner Andrey Kurkov (Diary of an Invasion) have attended our discussions and talked to us about their books and their writing. Members suggest books and vote on what to read next. Join us the second Thursday of the month in the Embarcadero Room. Here's our reading list since January 2023. October 7 - Trinket Trays; October 14 - Tote Bags; October 21 - Mini Pumpkins; October 28 - Bedazzling. Free supplies provided while they last. No registration—just show up and be ready to have fun!

events.title: Little Ones Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Wednesday mornings at 10:30 AM for Little Ones Storytime at Children's Library. Storytime includes a variety of early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, and movement activities. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. This program is targeted to children under the age of two and their caregivers.

events.description: Come join us for a set of STEM activities presented by Lynbrook High School's Women in STEM Club! Each month you'll explore a new set of topics as you learn about different fields of science and how they relate to the world. All materials will be provided. The experiments and demonstrations in this program are intended for an elementary-school-age audience. Parental supervision is required. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Try a set of hands-on STEM activities led by Lynbrook High School's Women in STEM Club, with new science topics each month.

events.title: Cupertino Spelling Bee
events.address: Cupertino Community Hall, 10350 Torre Ave, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is an annual contest for Cupertino students in grades 2-5, and is organized by the Cupertino Parks and Recreation Department and the Cupertino Youth Activity Board. Please note: The Cupertino Spelling Bee is not affiliated with the National Scripps Spelling Bee and we cannot sponsor or send winners to the National Spelling Bee. Registration will open with winter activity registration.

events.title: LEGO Club
events.description: Build and explore with tons of LEGO bricks. DUPLO bricks are also available for younger children. Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a LEGO Challenge. Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards. LEGO is a trademark of the LEGO Group. The LEGO Group does not sponsor, authorize or endorse this event or website.
events.blurb: Build with piles of LEGO bricks, with Duplo for younger kids, and ask the librarian for a Lego Challenge if you want something harder.

events.title: Community Threads: Holiday Placemat
events.description: In this workshop, folks will learn how to make a festive holiday placemat to decorate their homes for the holidays. You should know how to thread the machine, fill the bobbin, and use the backstitch, and you should understand the various other parts and functions of the sewing machine. Open to teens and adults only.

events.title: Saturday Board Games Day
events.description: Drop in for a full day of modern board gaming at the Downtown Library! The group meets every 1st Saturday from 10 AM–6 PM. Attendees can bring their own games to play or jump in with others. Please bring your own snacks and drinks to fuel an afternoon of marathon gaming in the El Camino Room. Presented by The Bay Area Boardgames Meetup Group. Masks are not required in the Palo Alto Libraries, but are recommended.

events.description: The open rehearsal features the erhu, a traditional Chinese two-stringed bowed instrument often called the Chinese violin. The public can watch the group prepare for an upcoming performance and take part in a Q&A. Stanley Wong, Ming Tsai, and Joyce Lin of the Harmony Chinese Chamber Orchestra lead the 50+ series.
events.blurb: Sit in on an open rehearsal featuring the erhu, the two-stringed bowed Chinese instrument often called the Chinese violin.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One-on-One Computer Help
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as printing, using email, connecting to Wi-Fi, creating documents, and accessing library resources such as e-books. We can also provide basic instructions for using devices such as laptops, smartphones, and e-readers. Free. No registration or appointment required. Just drop by and ask for assistance.

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Learn the basics of Taiwanese Mahjong or brush up on your skills with other adults and seniors. As you play, you'll learn how to set up and identify the tiles, follow the flow of play, make sets, and win the game. Did you know? Playing Mahjong helps improve cognitive function, helps reduce stress, and creates a sense of community. No registration needed.

events.description: Embrace a vibrant life at 50 and beyond! Join the Cupertino Senior Center for the Live Well Age Well Health Expo designed for individuals ages 50 and better. events.title: Housing Resource Navigator Drop-in Hours
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Get help finding shelter and other services you need. Meet with a peer navigator from The United Effort Organization who can help you find resources, sign up for services, connect with your support team, and take steps toward stable housing. events.title: Weekly Citizenship Class
events.description: Beginning your path to citizenship? Join us for a class series on the naturalization process, U.S. history and government, and English skills for the citizenship interview. Course information: Every Wednesday, 5:30-6:30 PM, 11/4/26-12/16/26. Each week we will cover a different portion of the application process and practice new skills. No class 11/25/26.
events.blurb: Learn about the naturalization process, U.S. history and government, and English skills for the citizenship interview in a weekly class series.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club: Intermediate
events.description: Free. In-person. No registration required. Suitable for intermediate English learners. We invite you to practice your English speaking and listening skills through our weekly conversation club! Each session is conducted in person by a library volunteer. A prompt will be given at the time of instruction, allowing for unscripted conversation beyond the textbook.
events.blurb: Practice English speaking and listening with a library volunteer through a guided weekly conversation prompt.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: Barbara Trent's documentary uses archival footage and interviews to examine the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama and American news coverage of it. The United Nations Association Film Festival screens documentaries on current issues. Jasmina Bojic, a Stanford lecturer and the festival's founder and director, leads discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.attendanceNote: The library's booking panel says registration is required. The event description says signup is optional. Reserve a seat through the library calendar or confirm with Rinconada Library.
events.blurb: Watch Barbara Trent's documentary The Panama Deception, which uses archival footage and interviews to examine the 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama and its news coverage.

This program is supported by Friends of Village Square Branch Library.
events.blurb: Get homework and class projects done on Monday afternoons with basic school supplies, snacks, and volunteers on hand to help with assignments.

No registration required.

events.description: Get help borrowing ebooks and audiobooks with Libby, connecting to Wi-Fi, navigating the library website, or printing at the library.

events.title: Winter Reading Bingo
events.description: Get ready to cozy up with a good book during the Winter Reading program, from December 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026. This free program invites readers of all ages to explore new stories, make time for reading, and earn a prize. Prize pickup is January 2, 2027, through January 10, 2027.
events.blurb: Readers of all ages can play Winter Reading Bingo for free at Milpitas Library and earn a prize.

events.title: Stanford Football vs SMU | Senior Day + Fan Appreciation
events.description: Stanford hosts SMU at Stanford Stadium for Senior Day and its Fan Appreciation Game.
events.blurb: Watch Stanford take on SMU at Stanford Stadium as the Cardinal honors its seniors.

events.title: Breathing & Meditation: The Natural Path to Better Immunity and Restful Sleep
events.description: Experience the soothing calm of meditation presented by library partner, Art of Living Foundation. Enjoy this free, one-hour session focused on managing stress and anxiety through simple, evidence-based techniques. These sessions are open to all adults and include optional light physical movement, breathing practices, and guided meditation. No prior experience is necessary. The agenda for a typical one-hour session is as follows: Optional Yoga Stretches (10 minutes): Light, beginner-friendly stretches; Will be offered based on participant interest. Breathing Techniques (10 minutes): Guided practice of calming breathwork; Techniques that can be used daily to reduce stress. Guided Meditation (20 minutes): Deep relaxation and mindfulness practice; Designed to calm the mind and promote inner peace. Experience Sharing & Program Info (10 minutes): Participants may share experiences; Information about the Art of Living and wellness programs; Optional: 3-minute video clip of past participant testimonials (if AV available). This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Registration is online.
events.blurb: Join an online one-hour session on breathing and meditation techniques for managing stress and anxiety, led by the Art of Living Foundation.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club - Hillview
events.description: Join us to practice, build, and strengthen your English-speaking skills. This is a fun, welcoming and respectful environment for adult English learners. Club meetings are held weekly and led online by a trained facilitator. Our dedicated and experienced volunteer, Patricia, leads the program and will help you build confidence in your English-speaking abilities. Please be sure to register by clicking the Register button. By providing your email address, you will receive the Zoom meeting link before the program begins.
events.blurb: A trained facilitator leads this weekly online conversation club for adults who want to practice speaking English.

events.title: Volunteer in the Heritage Rose Garden!
events.description: Help revitalize the largest public rose collection in the Western Hemisphere by weeding, deadheading, pruning, and planting seasonally. We suggest bringing a full water bottle and thick work gloves. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger. School groups or corporate teams must contact the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteer@grpg.org to schedule events. Park at 438 Coleman Ave., San Jose, CA 95110, and meet at the Rose Garden Shed. See the registration form for a map. The group meets every Saturday from 8:30 AM to 11:30 AM.
events.attendanceNote: Advance registration is required through Guadalupe River Park Conservancy. Meet at Rose Garden Shed; see the organizer's registration form for the meeting map. Chaperones are required for those age 15 and younger.
events.blurb: Weed, deadhead, prune, and help with seasonal planting among the roses in the Heritage Rose Garden on Saturday mornings.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. Beginners are welcome, and you don't need a partner. You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you'll get a reminder email with a link to the class playlist for practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps to international music with Sandy and Kent. You don't need a partner or any experience.

events.title: FOPAL Book Sale
events.description: At the Friends of the Palo Alto Library book sale, browse three rooms of new and gently used items, including books, CDs, DVDs, and puzzles. Everything is sorted and reasonably priced. Proceeds benefit the Palo Alto libraries. For the safety and comfort of all participants, masks are suggested and room occupancy will be lower than usual. Please visit fopal.org for more information. On Saturday, the Bargain Room is open from 9:30 AM to 4 PM, the Children's Room from 10 AM to 4 PM, and the Main Room from 11 AM to 4 PM. On Sunday, all rooms are open from 1 PM to 4 PM.
events.blurb: Browse the Friends of the Palo Alto Library book sale for books, CDs, DVDs and puzzles, with proceeds benefiting local libraries.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Night Hike and Flashlight Tour
events.description: Enjoy a fun-filled Night Hike and Flashlight Tour of McClellan Ranch Preserve and Blackberry Farm! We will explore the woods and nature at night, learn about nocturnal animals' special adaptations, and test our heightened senses in the dark with games and activities. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. Please wear appropriate walking shoes and a warm jacket and bring a flashlight or head-lamp. Everyone must register. Children must be accompanied by an adult. Admission is $10 for residents and $13 for nonresidents.
events.attendanceNote: All attendees must register. Children must be accompanied by an adult.
events.blurb: Walk McClellan Ranch Preserve after dark with a ranger, learning how nocturnal animals adapt to nighttime.

events.title: Sweetheart Social
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: Celebrate Valentine's Day with a memorable family night out at our Sweetheart Social! This event is the perfect way to make Valentine's Day feel extra special for you and your loved ones. Enjoy an evening filled with hands-on Valentine crafts, fun games and activities, a sweet treat, and a keepsake photo! Create sweet, lasting memories, and treat your family to a night of love and laughter. Registration will open with winter activity registration.
events.blurb: Spend a Valentine's Day family night out at the Sweetheart Social at Quinlan Community Center.

events.title: Family concert: Dave Rocha Jazz Trio 'Adventures in Jazz' for children
events.description: Dave Rocha Jazz Trio returns for a children's concert! Adventures in Jazz is a musical program that is fun, entertaining, and educational. Performed by talented and experienced jazz musicians, our show opens wide the doors of jazz music to young minds. For many, this will be their very first exposure to jazz music. We have performed for more than 15,000 students throughout the greater San Francisco Bay Area. Please join us for this enchanting concert.
events.blurb: Hear the Dave Rocha Jazz Trio play Adventures in Jazz, a children's concert that introduces young listeners to jazz music.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Cupertino Café
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 N Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: Teens, need a productive place to study? The Youth Activity Board is opening the Quinlan Community Center's banquet hall for a special teen study space. Enjoy free Panda Express, snacks, and coffee while you settle in and prepare for exams. When you're ready for a break, unwind with recreational games and calming activities. Cupertino Café is free, but please RSVP so we know how much food to order.
events.attendanceNote: The city asks teens to RSVP so it can plan food.
events.blurb: Study for exams in the Quinlan Community Center banquet hall, set up as a teen study space with free Panda Express, snacks, and coffee.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

events.title: JANE! An intimate exploration of Gilded Age excess and the enigmatic life and death of Jane Stanford
events.attendanceNote: Museum hours: Mon & Fri: 11 AM–6 PM; Thurs: 11 AM–8 PM; Sat & Sun: 10 AM–5 PM. Closed: Tues and Wed. The museum is closed Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving.
events.description: Curated by Associate Curator of European Art Patrick R. Crowley, JANE! celebrates the aesthetic and affective excesses of Jane Stanford, the Gilded Age founder and matriarch of Stanford University.
events.blurb: Tour the Cantor Arts Center exhibit on Jane Stanford's Gilded Age excess and mysterious death.

events.title: Electric Contrasts: the Art of the Detail
events.description: Electric Contrasts: The Art of the Detail brings together photobooks and magazines to show how the revolution of photography in the late 19th and early 20th centuries changed the history of art.
events.attendanceNote: Bowes Art & Architecture Library is closed Saturdays. Check the event calendar for hours. Visitors are asked to call 650-723-3408 for building and elevator access. Bowes Art & Architecture Library is closed November 26 through 29.
events.blurb: Browse photobooks and magazines tracing how early photography reshaped art history at the McMurtry Building.

events.title: Patty Chang: surfacing
events.description: In surfacing, Patty Chang engages the ocean as a physical, geopolitical, and symbolic space, inviting you to consider the work of collection and recollection.
events.attendanceNote: The museum is closed Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving.
events.blurb: See Patty Chang's surfacing, an exhibit treating the ocean as a physical, geopolitical and symbolic space tied to collection and recollection.

events.title: California Current: Art and Histories from the Bay Area
